scenes.vo: Still trying to guess where gold goes next?
Goldmap EA doesn’t predict. It runs the same six-step cycle on gold, inside your own MetaTrader.
One: it waits for its own structure condition on gold, then places the first position by itself.
Two: every open position goes into one basket. It watches total exposure, not one trade at a time.
Three: if price goes against the basket, built-in recovery rules adjust the plan instead of panicking.
Four: take profit is calculated for the whole basket. Once it’s reached, everything closes together.
Five: reset, wait for the next valid condition. Same routine, day after day.
Six: around rollover and thin-liquidity hours, new entries pause.
Plus a lot cap, equity guard, spread filter, and an optional daily target that stops new cycles.
Want to see it for yourself? Tap Get Goldmap EA at goldmapea.com.
Everyone shows you the upside. Let’s do the other side.
Goldmap EA lets you set a daily profit target. Say 1.5 percent, on a five-thousand-dollar account.
The upside panel assumes you win every single day. The website itself says that doesn’t happen in real trading, so we’re skipping it.
Now the other side. One bad basket costing thirty percent leaves five thousand at thirty-five hundred.
To get back to even, you now need plus forty-two point nine percent. Not thirty.
At a 1.5 percent target, that’s roughly 24 winning days just to climb back.
That’s why the lot cap and equity guard in the settings matter more than the target itself.
Try the calculator yourself, then tap Get Goldmap EA at goldmapea.com. Only run money you can genuinely afford to lose.
